Data sources

Source: vignettes/articles/data-sources.Rmd
data-sources.Rmd

Anything xarray can open, xrdbi can query. This article is a cookbook of sources: for each, which Python packages it needs and how to connect. Most recipes run live against public data. The Python environments article covers getting the packages.

library(xrdbi)
library(DBI)

dbConnect() takes exactly one of three things:

  • dsn, a string passed to an xarray open function: open_dataset() by default, or another named with open = ("open_zarr", "open_mfdataset", "open_datatree"). Other named arguments pass through as Python keyword arguments.
  • builder, an R function given the xarray module that returns a Dataset, for anything that takes more than one call.
  • object, a Dataset that already exists in the Python session.

A local netCDF file

The netCDF4 engine is declared when xrdbi loads, so local netCDF-3 and netCDF-4 files need nothing more:

f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/trmm.nc", package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)
dbGetInfo(con)$sizes
#> $time
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $latitude
#> [1] 40
#> 
#> $longitude
#> [1] 40
dbDisconnect(con)

netCDF over HTTPS

h5netcdf reads netCDF-4 (HDF5) files over HTTPS by byte ranges, through fsspec. One day of NOAA’s OISST sea surface temperature from NCEI:

reticulate::py_require(c("h5netcdf", "h5py", "fsspec", "aiohttp"))
oisst <- "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/sea-surface-temperature-optimum-interpolation/v2.1/access/avhrr/198109/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.19810901.nc"
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), oisst, engine = "h5netcdf")
dbGetQuery(con, "ds.sst.sel(lat=slice(-56, -55), lon=slice(100, 101))")
#>                   time zlev     lat     lon         sst
#> 1  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.875 100.125 -0.06000000
#> 2  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.875 100.375 -0.14000000
#> 3  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.875 100.625 -0.17000000
#> 4  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.875 100.875 -0.11000000
#> 5  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.625 100.125  0.06000000
#> 6  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.625 100.375  0.00000000
#> 7  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.625 100.625  0.01000000
#> 8  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.625 100.875  0.09999999
#> 9  1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.375 100.125  0.19000000
#> 10 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.375 100.375  0.17999999
#> 11 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.375 100.625  0.22999999
#> 12 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.375 100.875  0.34999999
#> 13 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.125  0.32999998
#> 14 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.375  0.34000000
#> 15 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.625  0.38999999
#> 16 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.875  0.50000000
dbDisconnect(con)

Many files as one dataset

open_mfdataset() combines files along their shared dimensions. It needs dask, and its variables are dask-backed, so a statement that computes stays lazy until fetched. A builder passes the list of files:

reticulate::py_require("dask")
days <- sprintf("https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/sea-surface-temperature-optimum-interpolation/v2.1/access/avhrr/198109/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.198109%02d.nc", 1:2)
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), builder = function(xr) {
  xr$open_mfdataset(days, engine = "h5netcdf")
})
dbGetInfo(con)$sizes
#> $time
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $zlev
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $lat
#> [1] 720
#> 
#> $lon
#> [1] 1440
dbGetQuery(con, "ds.sst.sel(lat=-55.125, lon=100.125)")
#>                  time zlev     lat     lon  sst
#> 1 1981-09-01 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.125 0.33
#> 2 1981-09-02 12:00:00    0 -55.125 100.125 0.48
dbDisconnect(con)

zarr on Google Cloud

zarr stores on Google Cloud Storage need zarr and gcsfs, and storage_options reaches gcsfs; token = "anon" reads a public bucket without credentials. The ARCO ERA5 reanalysis:

reticulate::py_require(c("zarr", "gcsfs"))
era <- "gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3"
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), era, engine = "zarr",
                 storage_options = reticulate::dict(token = "anon"))
con
#> <XarrayConnection>
#>   dsn: gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3
#>   dims: time: 1323648, latitude: 721, longitude: 1440, level: 37
#>   vars: 100m_u_component_of_wind, 100m_v_component_of_wind, ... (273 total)
dbGetQuery(con,
  "ds['2m_temperature'].sel(time='1980-01-01T00', latitude=-42.75,
                            longitude=147.25)")
#>   latitude longitude       time 2m_temperature
#> 1   -42.75    147.25 1980-01-01       286.1443
dbDisconnect(con)

Leave chunks out, as here, for lazily indexed arrays and a fast connection: sel() and isel() then read only the chunks they touch. chunks = reticulate::dict() (Python chunks={}) wraps every variable in dask at the storage chunking, which for a store of 273 variables in 1.3 million time chunks means minutes of graph building at connect time. open = "open_zarr" defaults to dask, so pass chunks = reticulate::py_none() with it.

zarr on S3

The same, with s3fs; anon = TRUE reads a public bucket. NASA’s MUR sea surface temperature on AWS (not run here: opening its metadata takes about a minute):

reticulate::py_require(c("zarr", "s3fs"))
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), "s3://mur-sst/zarr-v1", engine = "zarr",
                 storage_options = reticulate::dict(anon = TRUE))
dbGetQuery(con, "ds.analysed_sst.sel(time='2020-01-01', lat=-42.5,
                                     lon=147.5, method='nearest')")

Anything GDAL reads

The gdalxarray engine opens anything GDAL can, through GDAL’s virtual file systems (/vsicurl/, /vsis3/, …). It needs the GDAL Python bindings, which pip cannot install (see Python environments). A Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF over HTTPS, opened as a classic raster (multidim = FALSE), so that its bands are one variable, band_data:

tci <- "/vsicurl/https://sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sentinel-s2-l2a-cogs/36/Q/WD/2020/7/S2A_36QWD_20200701_0_L2A/TCI.tif"
cog <- dbConnect(xarray(), tci, engine = "gdalxarray", multidim = FALSE)
cog
#> <XarrayConnection>
#>   dsn: /vsicurl/https://sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sentinel-s2-l2a-cogs/36/Q/WD/2020/7/S2A_36QWD_20200701_0_L2A/TCI.tif
#>   dims: band: 3, y: 10980, x: 10980
#>   vars: band_data
dbGetQuery(cog, "ds.band_data.isel(y=5000, x=slice(5000, 5003))")
#>   band      x       y crs band_data
#> 1    1 549985 1850015   0       203
#> 2    1 549995 1850015   0       212
#> 3    1 550005 1850015   0       227
#> 4    2 549985 1850015   0       163
#> 5    2 549995 1850015   0       161
#> 6    2 550005 1850015   0       169
#> 7    3 549985 1850015   0       115
#> 8    3 549995 1850015   0       115
#> 9    3 550005 1850015   0       118
dbDisconnect(cog)

By default gdalxarray uses GDAL’s multidimensional API, which suits netCDF, HDF5, zarr and multidimensional VRTs. This VRT mosaics the whole daily OISST record, published by a scheduled pipeline. Its sources are in a public S3 bucket, so GDAL needs AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST:

Sys.setenv(AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST = "YES")
vrt <- "/vsicurl/https://projects.pawsey.org.au/aad-index/oisst/oisst-mdim.vrt"
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), vrt, engine = "gdalxarray")
con
#> <XarrayConnection>
#>   dsn: /vsicurl/https://projects.pawsey.org.au/aad-index/oisst/oisst-mdim.vrt
#>   dims: time: 16492, zlev: 1, lat: 720, lon: 1440
#>   vars: anom, err, ice, sst
dbGetQuery(con, "ds.time.isel(time=-1)")
#>                  time
#> 1 2026-10-26 12:00:00

GDAL reads its configuration from the process environment when it accesses data, so Sys.setenv() works even after Python has started, and a missing setting fails at the first query, not at connect: opening reads only the VRT. gdalxarray also takes config_options, a dict of GDAL options applied around the open and every read.

A connection is a snapshot. This VRT gains a day on a schedule, and a connection made before that keeps answering from the old version; a new connection sees the new day. For a record that does not move, open a dated version: oisst-mdim-20260630.vrt, beside it, holds the days to the end of June 2026.

dbDisconnect(con)

Icechunk and virtual stores

A builder covers sources that take more than one call: kerchunk or VirtualiZarr references, or an icechunk repository. Icechunk versions a zarr store, and a readonly session at a branch, tag or snapshot is a fixed version of the data.

This repository, on Source Cooperative, holds daily ocean salinity from the BRAN reanalysis as a virtual store: its metadata and coordinates are in the repository, and each data chunk is a byte range in the original netCDF files on NCI’s THREDDS server. Icechunk reads virtual chunks only from locations it is authorized for, so the builder authorizes that server, and caps concurrent requests, since THREDDS resets connections above about ten:

reticulate::py_require(c("icechunk", "zarr"))
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), builder = function(xr) {
  ic <- reticulate::import("icechunk", convert = FALSE)
  storage <- ic$s3_storage(
    bucket = "us-west-2.opendata.source.coop",
    prefix = "ausantarctic/ausantarctic-scratch/bluelink/bluelink-daily-salt/icechunk",
    region = "us-west-2", anonymous = TRUE)
  config <- ic$Repository$fetch_config(storage)
  config$max_concurrent_requests <- 4L
  repo <- ic$Repository$open(storage, config = config,
    authorize_virtual_chunk_access = reticulate::dict(
      "https://thredds.nci.org.au/" = ic$credentials$HttpAccess))
  xr$open_zarr(repo$readonly_session("main")$store, consolidated = FALSE,
               chunks = reticulate::py_none())
})
con
#> <XarrayConnection>
#>   dims: Time: 12265, st_ocean: 51, yt_ocean: 1500, xt_ocean: 3600
#>   vars: salt

Each chunk of salt is one day at one depth over a 300 by 300 cell block, so a value at the surface is one range request:

dbGetQuery(con, "ds.salt.sel(Time='2020-01-01', st_ocean=0, yt_ocean=-45,
                             xt_ocean=147.5, method='nearest')")
#>                  Time xt_ocean st_ocean yt_ocean     salt
#> 1 2020-01-01 12:00:00   147.45      2.5   -45.05 35.11521
dbDisconnect(con)

A Dataset built in Python

object = adopts a Dataset that already exists, however it was made:

reticulate::py_run_string("
import xarray, numpy
myds = xarray.Dataset({'v': (('y', 'x'), numpy.arange(6.).reshape(2, 3))},
                      coords={'y': [10, 20], 'x': [1, 2, 3]})
")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), object = reticulate::py_eval("myds", convert = FALSE))
dbGetQuery(con, "ds.v")
#>    y x v
#> 1 10 1 0
#> 2 10 2 1
#> 3 10 3 2
#> 4 20 1 3
#> 5 20 2 4
#> 6 20 3 5
dbDisconnect(con)

The connection holds a reference to the object itself, so changes made to it in place, such as myds['w'] = myds.v * 2, are seen by later queries. Binding the Python name to a new object is not: the connection keeps the object it was given.
